findings.title: New guard reimplements goType() and pins a []*T vs []T mismatch
findings.claim: reflect.TypeOf(info.Zero()) yields []*T while goType() (used by unmarshalList and reached via MapScan) yields []T; Scan(&any) gives []*float32 but MapScan gives []float32 for vector<float,3>, and the test at marshal_vector_test.go:928 freezes this inconsistency instead of using goType(info) which would be nil-safe and consistent.

findings.title: Nil-SubType comment overstates the protection it provides
findings.claim: unmarshalVector(VectorType{Dimensions: 3}, make([]byte,12), &dst) still nil-derefs in vectorFixedElemSize; the guard adds a second, earlier copy of the dereference under a comment that reads as if it were handled, though the report notes this is not a regression and not wire-reachable.

findings.title: math.MaxInt32 saturation branch has no test coverage
findings.claim: The saturation branch is the only overflow guard in the new arithmetic, but TestVectorElemMinSize only covers 0 and -3 dimensions, nothing large enough to trigger saturation; the report says it was verified correct by hand.

findings.title: Nested-vector error message still omits element type and dimensions
findings.claim: For the nested-vector case, the message still reports custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType) with no element type or dimensions, because the inner type is built with prefix+"VectorType" rather than name.

findings.title: vectorElemMinSize recomputed per value at O(depth²)
findings.claim: vectorElemMinSize is recomputed per value with quadratic cost relative to depth, measured at 2.7ms per 4-byte value for an 800-deep type; the report notes this is bounded in practice and dwarfed by a pre-existing quadratic type-name parse (38s for the same name).
